decisions.choice: the people are camped in the wilderness of Paran
decisions.reason: The chapter goes on from 12:16, where the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran. The command that follows comes there, near the southern edge of Canaan.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "envoya", "montèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "sont montés"); the scouts' report in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. The report in verses 27-33 is speech, so it uses the passé composé ("nous sommes allés", "nous avons vu") at every level.

en.L: "Send for yourself men, that they may spy out the land of Canaan, which I [am] giving to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. One man, one man for the tribe of his fathers you shall send, every one a leader among them."
en.B: "Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. From each ancestral tribe send one man, and each of them is to be a leader among them."

decisions.choice: spy out: go through a land to search it and report on it
decisions.reason: The verb means to go about, explore and search out. It is used for the scouts all through this story (verses 16, 17, 21, 25, 32) and for God going ahead to search out a camping place for Israel (10:33). The same verb comes back in 15:39, where Israel is told not to go about after its own heart and eyes.

decisions.choice: send for yourself: Moses is to send them, as his own mission
decisions.reason: The phrase "for yourself" marks the sending as Moses' own act. Deuteronomy 1:22-23 tells the same event from the other side: the people asked for scouts to be sent and Moses agreed. Here God gives the command, and the two accounts together show the plan coming from both.

decisions.choice: one man for each ancestral tribe, each a leader
decisions.reason: Every tribe is to be represented, so the report will come from the whole people. These leaders are not the same men as the tribal leaders named in 1:5-15 and 7:12-83; the word "leader" here means a man of rank in his tribe, not its chief.

decisions.choice: "for yourself" not rendered
decisions.reason: Natural English has no need of "for yourself" after "send", and saying it would suggest the men were to serve Moses privately. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: a leader in his tribe
decisions.reason: "Among them" refers back to the tribe each man comes from; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: "espiar" (L) and "explorar" (B, R) for the scouts' verb, through the chapter
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the sense of spying out a land held by others; Balanced and Readable use "explorar", the plain word for going through a land to search it, as the English says "scout out" and "explore".

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:enviarán|enviaréis}}" in the plural
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you will send" is plural, though the command opens to Moses alone; Literal and Balanced keep the plural, which Spanish can show. Readable says "Envía" to Moses, as the English Readable has a single command.

decisions.choice: "explorer" (L, R) and "reconnaître" (B) for the scouts' verb, through the chapter
decisions.reason: "Espionner" today suggests secret intelligence work. "Reconnaître le pays" is the usual French for scouting out ground ahead of an army, and suits Balanced; "explorer" is the plain word, used at Literal and Readable.

decisions.choice: "kupeleleza" (L, B) and "kuchunguza" (R) for the scouts' verb, through the chapter
decisions.reason: "Kupeleleza" is to spy out or reconnoitre, the scouts' task; Readable uses "kuchunguza", to examine or explore, the plainer word, as the English Readable says "explore".

decisions.choice: "do thám" (L, B); "đi xem xét" (R) for spy out
decisions.reason: The men go through the land to search it and report (meaning decision); "do thám" is the ordinary word for scouting a land, and Readable says it plainly. Kept through chapters 13-14.

decisions.choice: "chi tộc" for tribe; "thủ lĩnh" (L, B), "người lãnh đạo" (R) for leader; "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L), "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for these chapters. Vietnamese "con cháu" and "dân" already take in men and women, so the English gender setting has no Vietnamese counterpart. Recorded once for chapters 12-18.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L), "이스라엘 백성" (B), "이스라엘 사람들" (R); no gender span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy. The Korean words already include women and men, so Korean needs no gender span where the English has one. Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "정탐하다" (L, B); "살펴보다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is going through a land to search it and report (meaning decision); "정탐하다" is the standard word, and Readable uses the plain "살펴보다". The men are "정탐꾼" where they are named as a group.

decisions.choice: for the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur: the first of twelve entries
decisions.reason: Verses 4-15 list the twelve men in the same short form: the tribe, then the man and his father. The order is close to that of 1:5-15 but not the same: Zebulun and Manasseh come later, and Naphtali comes before Gad. Levi has no man, since it receives no share of the land (18:20-24).

decisions.choice: from the tribe
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for the tribe" means the man represents that tribe; "from the tribe" says the same in natural English. Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: the scouts' names transcribed by the book's conventions: "sh" for shin, "ou" for u, "k" for kaf and qof, "gu" before e and i ("Shammoua fils de Zakkour", "Guéouel", "Guemalli")
decisions.reason: Most of these men are named only here, so French has no fixed form for them. Their names follow the same transcription as the other minor names in this translation, so that a French reader can say them as the Hebrew sounds.

decisions.choice: names of the twelve men in their usual Protestant forms (Sam-mua, Xa-cu, Sa-phát, Hô-ri, Di-ganh, Hô-sê, Phan-ti, Ra-phu, Gát-đi-ên, Sô-đi, Ga-đi, Su-si, A-mi-ên, Ghê-ma-li, Sê-thu, Mi-ca-ên, Nách-bi, Vấp-si, Ghê-u-ên, Ma-ki)
decisions.reason: Names not in the term sheets follow the usual Protestant transliteration, as the sheets ask; "con trai" without "của" keeps a list of names short.

decisions.choice: "삭굴의 아들 삼무아": father's name first
decisions.reason: Korean puts the father before the son ("A의 아들 B"), the usual Korean order in genealogies; each entry of the list ends with a comma so the twelve read as one list.

decisions.choice: Hoshea: "he saves"; Joshua: "Yahweh saves"
decisions.reason: Both names come from the verb "to save". Moses adds the first part of the divine name to Hoshea's name, so that it says who saves. The Greek form of the name Joshua is "Jesus".

decisions.choice: called: the text does not say when the name was given
decisions.reason: Hoshea is already called Joshua in Exodus 17:9 and Numbers 11:28. The verse may record the renaming at this point, or note a name Moses had given him earlier. Either way, the man sent to scout the land will be the one who leads Israel into it.

decisions.choice: gave ... the name Joshua
decisions.reason: "Called Hoshea Joshua" is awkward in English. Balanced and Readable say Moses gave him the name, which keeps the open question of when it happened.

decisions.choice: "Hô-sê" and "Giô-suê"
decisions.reason: "Giô-suê" is the term sheet's form; "Hô-sê" keeps the h of the Hebrew so that it is not confused with the prophet Hosea ("Ô-sê"). The meanings of the two names are left to the meaning decision, as the English leaves them.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry country at the south of Canaan
decisions.reason: The word names the dry region south of the hill country, around Beersheba, and can also mean simply "south". Here it is the region the scouts enter first, coming up from the wilderness (verse 22; verse 29 says the Amalekites live there).

decisions.choice: the hill country: the central highlands of Canaan
decisions.reason: The hill country is the ridge of hills running north through the middle of the land, where Hebron and later Jerusalem stand. Verse 29 names the peoples who live there.

decisions.choice: this [way]: by this route, from where they now are
decisions.reason: The word "this" points to the way in front of them, going up from Paran and the region of Kadesh. It may also mean "here", as in "go up from here".

decisions.choice: Go north
decisions.reason: "Go up" means climbing from the wilderness into the higher land to the north. Readable says "north" so the direction is clear.

decisions.choice: Moses calls the men "các ngươi" (L), "anh em" (B, R), and himself "tôi"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for Moses speaking to Israel; the twelve leaders are addressed the same way. Recorded once for chapters 12-18.

decisions.choice: "Nê-ghép"; "miền đồi núi" for the hill country
decisions.reason: "Nê-ghép" as in the Vietnamese Genesis; "miền đồi núi" is the plain word for the central highlands (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to the twelve men in 해라체
decisions.reason: The men are sent on Moses' own mission as their leader (meaning decision), so he gives them orders in the plain style, as he speaks to Joshua in Exodus 17:9; they report back to him in 합쇼체 (verse 27).

decisions.choice: "네겝"; Readable "네겝 광야"
decisions.reason: The place name as Genesis 12:9 gives it in Korean; Readable adds "광야" for the dry country, as the English Readable adds "Desert".

vi.R: Hãy xem đất ở đó có tốt cho việc trồng trọt không, và có cây cối mọc ở đó không. Hãy can đảm và mang về một ít trái cây mọc trong xứ." Lúc ấy là thời điểm trong năm khi những chùm nho đầu tiên bắt đầu chín.

decisions.choice: fat or lean: rich or poor soil
decisions.reason: "Fat" land is fertile, land that yields good crops; "lean" land is thin and poor (Nehemiah 9:25, 35; Ezekiel 34:14).

decisions.choice: strengthen yourselves: take courage
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong. In this setting it means to act boldly, as men going into a land held by others. Words from the same root are used of courage in Deuteronomy 31:6 and Joshua 1:6-7.

decisions.choice: the days of the first ripe grapes: about midsummer
decisions.reason: In Canaan the first grapes ripen in the summer, around July. The note explains why the scouts could cut a cluster of grapes in verse 23.

decisions.choice: rich or poor / good for farming
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of the soil, which is what "fat" and "lean" describe. Literal keeps the Hebrew words.

decisions.choice: bring back
decisions.reason: "Take" fruit means taking it to bring home, as verse 26 shows.

decisions.choice: "màu mỡ hay cằn cỗi" for fat or lean
decisions.reason: Vietnamese says rich or poor soil with these two words, which is the sense of the Hebrew picture (meaning decision); "béo hay gầy" is not said of land.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ וַיָּתֻ֣רוּ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ מִמִּדְבַּר־צִ֥ן עַד־רְחֹ֖ב לְבֹ֥א חֲמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went up and spied out the land from [the] wilderness of Zin to Rehob, Lebo-hamath.

en.L: And they went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, at Lebo-hamath.
en.B: So they went up and scouted out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
en.R: So they went and explored the land, from the Zin Desert in the south all the way to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath in the far north.

es.L: Y subieron y espiaron la tierra desde el desierto de Zin hasta Rejob, en Lebo-jamat.
es.B: Subieron, pues, y exploraron la tierra desde el desierto de Zin hasta Rejob, cerca de Lebo-jamat.
es.R: Así que fueron y recorrieron la tierra, desde el desierto de Zin, en el sur, hasta Rejob, cerca de Lebo-jamat, en el extremo norte.

fr.L: Et ils montèrent et explorèrent le pays depuis le désert de Tsin jusqu’à Rehob, à Lebo-Hamath.
fr.B: Ils montèrent donc et reconnurent le pays, depuis le désert de Tsin jusqu’à Rehob, près de Lebo-Hamath.
fr.R: Ils sont donc partis explorer le pays, depuis le désert de Tsin, au sud, jusqu’à Rehob, près de Lebo-Hamath, tout au nord.

sw.L: Basi wakapanda wakaipeleleza nchi tangu nyika ya Zini mpaka Rehobu, huko Lebo-hamathi.
sw.B: Basi walipanda wakaipeleleza nchi kutoka nyika ya Zini mpaka Rehobu, karibu na Lebo-hamathi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo walikwenda wakaichunguza nchi, kutoka jangwa la Zini upande wa kusini mpaka Rehobu, karibu na Lebo-hamathi, kaskazini kabisa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 올라가서 신 광야에서부터 르보하맛의 르홉까지 그 땅을 정탐했다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 올라가서 신 광야에서부터 르보하맛 가까이에 있는 르홉까지 그 땅을 정탐했다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 가서 그 땅을 살펴보았다. 남쪽 신 광야에서부터 저 북쪽 르보하맛 가까이에 있는 르홉까지 다녔다.

vi.L: Và họ đi lên và do thám xứ từ hoang mạc Xin cho đến Rê-hốp, tại Lê-bô Ha-mát.
vi.B: Vậy họ đi lên và do thám xứ từ hoang mạc Xin cho đến Rê-hốp, gần Lê-bô Ha-mát.
vi.R: Vậy họ đi xem xét xứ, từ hoang mạc Xin ở phía nam cho đến Rê-hốp, gần Lê-bô Ha-mát ở tận phía bắc.

decisions.choice: from the wilderness of Zin to Lebo-hamath: the whole land, south to north
decisions.reason: The wilderness of Zin lies on the southern border of Canaan, and Lebo-hamath on the far northern border (34:3, 8). The scouts went through the whole length of the land. Rehob was a town in the north, toward Hamath (Judges 18:28 places a Beth-rehob near Dan).

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath: a place name, or "the entrance of Hamath"
decisions.reason: The words can be read as the name of a town, Lebo-hamath, or as "the way into Hamath", the pass leading to the land of Hamath in Syria. Either way the point is the northern edge of the land.

decisions.choice: in the south ... in the far north
decisions.reason: Readable adds the directions so the reader can see how far the scouts went.

decisions.choice: "Zini" for the wilderness of Zin
decisions.reason: Swahili usually writes the Hebrew ts as "s", but "jangwa la Sini" is already the wilderness of Sin in Exodus 16, a different place. "Zini" keeps the two apart, as French ("Tsin" and "Sin") and Spanish ("Zin" and "Sin") do.

decisions.choice: "Lê-bô Ha-mát" as a place name
decisions.reason: The English reads a place name and footnotes "the entrance of Hamath" (meaning decision); Vietnamese follows, with "Xin" and "Rê-hốp" in their usual Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "르보하맛" as a place name
decisions.reason: The English reads it as a place name, with "the entrance of Hamath" in the meaning decision's footnote; Korean follows the same reading. "신" is the wilderness of Zin, as Exodus 17:1 and Joshua 15:1 give it.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ בַנֶּגֶב֮ וַיָּבֹ֣א עַד־חֶבְרוֹן֒ וְשָׁ֤ם אֲחִימַן֙ שֵׁשַׁ֣י וְתַלְמַ֔י יְלִידֵ֖י הָעֲנָ֑ק וְחֶבְר֗וֹן שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ נִבְנְתָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י צֹ֥עַן מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went up into the Negev, and he came to Hebron, and there [were] Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, those born of the Anak; and Hebron seven years was built before Zoan of Egypt.

en.L: And they went up into the Negev, and he came to Hebron; and Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, those born of Anak, [were] there. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan of Egypt.)
en.B: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
en.R: They went up through the Negev Desert and came to the town of Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai lived there. They were descendants of Anak, a people known for being very tall. Hebron was built seven years before the city of Zoan in Egypt.

es.L: Y subieron por el Néguev, y llegó hasta Hebrón; y allí [estaban] Ahimán, Sesai y Talmai, los nacidos de Anac. (Y Hebrón fue edificada siete años antes que Zoán de Egipto.)
es.B: Subieron por el Néguev y llegaron a Hebrón, donde vivían Ahimán, Sesai y Talmai, descendientes de Anac. (Hebrón había sido fundada siete años antes que Zoán, en Egipto.)
es.R: Subieron por el desierto del Néguev y llegaron a la ciudad de Hebrón. Allí vivían Ahimán, Sesai y Talmai. Eran descendientes de Anac, un pueblo conocido por ser de muy alta estatura. Hebrón fue construida siete años antes que la ciudad de Zoán, en Egipto.

fr.L: Et ils montèrent dans le Néguev, et il vint jusqu’à Hébron ; et là [étaient] Ahimân, Shéshaï et Talmaï, ceux qui [étaient] nés d’Anaq. (Or Hébron avait été bâtie sept ans avant Tsoan d’Égypte.)
fr.B: Ils montèrent par le Néguev et arrivèrent à Hébron, où vivaient Ahimân, Shéshaï et Talmaï, les descendants d’Anaq. (Hébron avait été bâtie sept ans avant Tsoan, en Égypte.)
fr.R: Ils sont montés à travers le désert du Néguev et sont arrivés à la ville d’Hébron. Ahimân, Shéshaï et Talmaï vivaient là. C’étaient des descendants d’Anaq, un peuple connu pour sa très grande taille. Hébron avait été construite sept ans avant la ville de Tsoan, en Égypte.

sw.L: Nao wakapanda katika Negebu, naye akafika mpaka Hebroni; na huko [walikuwako] Ahimani, Sheshai na Talmai, waliozaliwa na Anaki. (Basi Hebroni ilijengwa miaka saba kabla ya Soani ya Misri.)
sw.B: Walipanda kupitia Negebu wakafika Hebroni, mahali walipoishi Ahimani, Sheshai na Talmai, wazao wa Anaki. (Hebroni ilikuwa imejengwa miaka saba kabla ya Soani huko Misri.)
sw.R: Walipanda kupitia jangwa la Negebu wakafika mji wa Hebroni. Ahimani, Sheshai na Talmai waliishi huko. Hao walikuwa wazao wa Anaki, watu waliojulikana kwa kuwa warefu sana. Mji wa Hebroni ulijengwa miaka saba kabla ya mji wa Soani huko Misri.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 네겝으로 올라갔고, 그가 헤브론에 이르렀다. 그런데 거기에 아낙의 자손들인 아히만과 세새와 달매가 있었다. (헤브론은 이집트의 소안보다 칠 년 먼저 세워졌다.)
ko.B: 그들은 네겝을 거쳐 올라가 헤브론에 이르렀다. 그곳에는 아낙의 자손인 아히만과 세새와 달매가 살고 있었다. (헤브론은 이집트의 소안보다 칠 년 먼저 세워진 곳이다.)
ko.R: 그들은 네겝 광야를 지나 올라가서 헤브론 성읍에 이르렀다. 그곳에는 아히만과 세새와 달매가 살고 있었다. 그들은 몸집이 아주 큰 것으로 알려진 아낙 사람들의 자손이었다. 헤브론은 이집트의 소안 성보다 칠 년 먼저 세워졌다.

vi.L: Và họ đi lên vào Nê-ghép, và đến Hếp-rôn; và A-hi-man, Sê-sai và Thanh-mai, những người sinh ra từ A-nác, [ở] tại đó. (Vả, Hếp-rôn đã được xây bảy năm trước Xô-an của Ai Cập.)
vi.B: Họ đi lên qua miền Nê-ghép và đến Hếp-rôn, nơi A-hi-man, Sê-sai và Thanh-mai, dòng dõi của A-nác, sinh sống. (Hếp-rôn đã được xây dựng bảy năm trước thành Xô-an ở Ai Cập.)
vi.R: Họ đi lên qua hoang mạc Nê-ghép và đến thành Hếp-rôn. A-hi-man, Sê-sai và Thanh-mai sống ở đó. Họ là dòng dõi của A-nác, một dân nổi tiếng là rất cao lớn. Hếp-rôn được xây dựng bảy năm trước thành Xô-an ở Ai Cập.

decisions.choice: he came: a singular verb in the middle of plural ones
decisions.reason: The other verbs are plural ("they went up"), but "came" is singular. It may treat the group as one, or it may mean that one of the scouts came to Hebron, perhaps Caleb, to whom the land of Hebron is later given because he followed the LORD fully (14:24; Joshua 14:9, 13-14).

decisions.choice: those born of the Anak: the Anakim, a people known for their size
decisions.reason: The phrase means the descendants of Anak, or of "the Anak", since the word has the article here. The Anakim were remembered as very tall (verses 28, 32-33; Deuteronomy 2:10; 9:2). Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai are driven out of Hebron by Caleb in Joshua 15:14.

decisions.choice: Hebron was built seven years before Zoan
decisions.reason: Zoan was a city in the eastern Nile delta, later known as Tanis. The note shows how old Hebron was, the place where Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had lived and were buried (Genesis 23:2, 19; 35:27). Hebron was also called Kiriath-arba (Joshua 14:15).

decisions.choice: came (no separate subject)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they ... came", because a lone "he" would read as a mistake in English. Literal keeps "he", and a footnote gives the question.

decisions.choice: a people known for being very tall
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the descendants of Anak were, from verses 28 and 32-33, since the rest of the story turns on it.

decisions.choice: "và đến Hếp-rôn" with no subject (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not mark number, so the singular "he came" (meaning decision, footnoted) cannot be shown without naming a subject the Hebrew does not name; Literal leaves the subject out.

decisions.choice: "A-nác", "A-hi-man, Sê-sai và Thanh-mai", "Xô-an"
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Joshua 15:13-14 and the usual Protestant "Xô-an" for Zoan.

decisions.choice: "그가 이르렀다" (L); no separate subject at B and R
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular verb the meaning decision notes, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable let the plural subject run on, since Korean need not repeat the subject.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַד־נַ֣חַל אֶשְׁכֹּ֗ל וַיִּכְרְת֨וּ מִשָּׁ֤ם זְמוֹרָה֙ וְאֶשְׁכּ֤וֹל עֲנָבִים֙ אֶחָ֔ד וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֥הוּ בַמּ֖וֹט בִּשְׁנָ֑יִם וּמִן־הָרִמֹּנִ֖ים וּמִן־הַתְּאֵנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] valley of Eshcol, and they cut down from there [a] branch and [a] cluster of grapes, one, and they carried it on [a] pole by two, and from the pomegranates and from the figs.

en.L: And they came to the Valley of Eshcol, and they cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they carried it on a pole between two [men], and [they took] some of the pomegranates and some of the figs.
en.B: When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut off a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and two of them carried it on a pole. They also took some of the pomegranates and figs.
en.R: When they came to the Eshcol Valley, they cut off a branch that had just one bunch of grapes on it. Two men carried it on a pole between them. They also took some pomegranates and figs.

es.L: Y llegaron hasta el valle de Escol, y cortaron de allí un sarmiento con un racimo de uvas, uno solo, y lo llevaron en una vara entre dos [hombres], y [tomaron] de las granadas y de los higos.
es.B: Al llegar al valle de Escol, cortaron un sarmiento con un solo racimo de uvas, y dos de ellos lo llevaron colgado de una vara. También tomaron algunas granadas e higos.
es.R: Cuando llegaron al valle de Escol, cortaron una rama que tenía un solo racimo de uvas. Dos hombres la cargaron en un palo entre los dos. También se llevaron algunas granadas e higos.

fr.L: Et ils vinrent jusqu’à la vallée d’Eshkol, et ils coupèrent de là un sarment avec une grappe de raisins, une seule, et ils la portèrent sur une perche à deux [hommes], et [ils prirent] des grenades et des figues.
fr.B: Arrivés à la vallée d’Eshkol, ils coupèrent un sarment portant une seule grappe de raisins, et deux d’entre eux le portèrent sur une perche. Ils prirent aussi des grenades et des figues.
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés à la vallée d’Eshkol, ils ont coupé une branche de vigne qui portait une seule grappe de raisins. Deux hommes l’ont portée sur une perche, entre eux. Ils ont aussi pris des grenades et des figues.

sw.L: Nao wakafika mpaka bonde la Eshkoli, wakakata huko tawi lenye kishada kimoja cha zabibu, wakakibeba kwa mti kati ya [watu] wawili, na [wakachukua] baadhi ya makomamanga na baadhi ya tini.
sw.B: Walipofika bonde la Eshkoli, walikata tawi lenye kishada kimoja tu cha zabibu, na wawili kati yao wakalibeba kwa mti. Pia wakachukua baadhi ya makomamanga na tini.
sw.R: Walipofika bonde la Eshkoli, walikata tawi lililokuwa na kishada kimoja tu cha zabibu. Watu wawili walilibeba kwa mti katikati yao. Walichukua pia makomamanga na tini.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 에스골 골짜기에 이르러, 거기서 포도송이 하나가 달린 가지를 잘라, 그것을 두 [사람이] 막대기에 [꿰어] 메었다. 그리고 석류와 무화과도 얼마 [가져왔다].
ko.B: 그들은 에스골 골짜기에 이르러, 포도송이 하나가 달린 가지를 잘라서 두 사람이 막대기에 꿰어 메고 왔다. 또 석류와 무화과도 얼마 가져왔다.
ko.R: 그들은 에스골 골짜기에 이르러 포도가 한 송이 달린 가지를 잘랐다. 두 사람이 그것을 막대기에 꿰어 함께 메었다. 그들은 석류와 무화과도 조금 땄다.

vi.L: Và họ đến thung lũng Ếch-côn, và từ đó họ cắt một nhánh [nho] với một chùm nho, và họ khiêng nó bằng một đòn giữa hai [người], và [họ lấy] một ít trái lựu và một ít trái vả.
vi.B: Khi đến thung lũng Ếch-côn, họ cắt một nhánh nho chỉ có một chùm, và hai người phải khiêng chùm nho ấy bằng một cây đòn. Họ cũng lấy một ít trái lựu và trái vả.
vi.R: Khi đến thung lũng Ếch-côn, họ cắt một nhánh nho chỉ có một chùm. Hai người phải khiêng nó bằng một cây đòn đặt giữa họ. Họ cũng lấy một ít trái lựu và trái vả.

decisions.choice: valley: a wadi, a valley with a stream bed
decisions.reason: The word names a valley whose stream runs in the rainy season and dries up in summer. Such valleys were often good for vines.

decisions.choice: one cluster carried on a pole by two men
decisions.reason: The text stresses that it was a single cluster, yet two men carried it on a pole between them. The point is how large and heavy it was, a sign of how rich the land is (verse 27).

decisions.choice: [men] / [they took]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "by two" and "and from the pomegranates". Literal supplies the missing words in brackets; Balanced supplies them without.

decisions.choice: "thung lũng Ếch-côn"
decisions.reason: The valley has a stream bed (meaning decision); "thung lũng" is the common word, and "Ếch-côn" the form of the Vietnamese Genesis 14:13.

source.text: לַמָּק֣וֹם הַה֔וּא קָרָ֖א נַ֣חַל אֶשְׁכּ֑וֹל עַ֚ל אֹד֣וֹת הָֽאֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־כָּרְת֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: That place one called Valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which cut down from there [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: That place was called the Valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster that the sons of Israel cut down from there.
en.B: That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut there.
en.R: That place was named the Eshcol Valley, which means Cluster Valley, because of the bunch of grapes the Israelites cut there.

es.L: A aquel lugar se le llamó valle de Escol, a causa del racimo que cortaron de allí los hijos de Israel.
es.B: A aquel lugar lo llamaron valle de Escol por el racimo de uvas que los israelitas cortaron allí.
es.R: Ese lugar recibió el nombre de valle de Escol, que significa «valle del Racimo», por el racimo de uvas que los israelitas cortaron allí.

fr.L: Ce lieu-là, on l’appela vallée d’Eshkol, à cause de la grappe que les fils d’Israël y coupèrent.
fr.B: On appela ce lieu la vallée d’Eshkol, à cause de la grappe de raisins que les Israélites y avaient coupée.
fr.R: Cet endroit a reçu le nom de vallée d’Eshkol, ce qui veut dire « vallée de la Grappe », à cause de la grappe de raisins que les Israélites y avaient coupée.

sw.L: Mahali pale paliitwa bonde la Eshkoli, kwa sababu ya kishada ambacho wana wa Israeli walikikata kutoka huko.
sw.B: Mahali pale paliitwa bonde la Eshkoli kwa sababu ya kishada cha zabibu ambacho Waisraeli walikata huko.
sw.R: Mahali pale paliitwa bonde la Eshkoli, maana yake "Bonde la Kishada", kwa sababu ya kishada cha zabibu ambacho Waisraeli walikata huko.

ko.L: 그 곳을 에스골 골짜기라고 불렀는데, 이스라엘 자손이 거기서 잘라 낸 포도송이 때문이었다.
ko.B: 그곳을 에스골 골짜기라고 부르게 된 것은, 이스라엘 백성이 거기서 포도송이를 잘랐기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 그곳을 '송이 골짜기'라는 뜻의 에스골 골짜기라고 불렀다. 이스라엘 사람들이 거기서 포도송이를 잘랐기 때문이다.

vi.L: Nơi ấy được gọi là thung lũng Ếch-côn, vì cớ chùm [nho] mà con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cắt từ đó.
vi.B: Nơi ấy được gọi là thung lũng Ếch-côn, vì chùm nho mà dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cắt tại đó.
vi.R: Nơi ấy được đặt tên là thung lũng Ếch-côn, nghĩa là "thung lũng Chùm Nho", vì chùm nho mà dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cắt ở đó.

decisions.choice: Eshcol: "cluster"
decisions.reason: The place name is the same word as "cluster" in verse 23. The verse explains the name by the cluster of grapes. Eshcol is also the name of a man living near Hebron in Abraham's time (Genesis 14:13, 24).

decisions.choice: one called: the place was called, without naming who named it
decisions.reason: The verb is active with no subject, a common Hebrew way of saying "it was called".

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel / the Israelites, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: Here "the sons of Israel" are the twelve scouts, all men, so the wording takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: which means Cluster Valley
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name, which the verse depends on.

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ מִתּ֣וּר הָאָ֑רֶץ מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they returned from spying out the land at [the] end of forty days.

en.L: And they returned from spying out the land at the end of forty days.
en.B: After forty days they came back from scouting out the land.
en.R: After forty days of exploring the land, they came back.

es.L: Y volvieron de espiar la tierra al cabo de cuarenta días.
es.B: Al cabo de cuarenta días regresaron de explorar la tierra.
es.R: Después de recorrer la tierra durante cuarenta días, volvieron.

fr.L: Et ils revinrent d’explorer le pays au bout de quarante jours.
fr.B: Au bout de quarante jours, ils revinrent après avoir reconnu le pays.
fr.R: Après avoir exploré le pays pendant quarante jours, ils sont revenus.

sw.L: Nao wakarudi kutoka kuipeleleza nchi mwisho wa siku arobaini.
sw.B: Baada ya siku arobaini walirudi kutoka kuipeleleza nchi.
sw.R: Baada ya kuichunguza nchi kwa siku arobaini, walirudi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 사십 일이 끝날 때에 그 땅을 정탐하는 데서 돌아왔다.
ko.B: 사십 일 뒤에 그들은 그 땅을 정탐하고 돌아왔다.
ko.R: 그들은 사십 일 동안 그 땅을 살펴보고 돌아왔다.

vi.L: Và họ trở về từ việc do thám xứ vào cuối bốn mươi ngày.
vi.B: Sau bốn mươi ngày do thám xứ, họ trở về.
vi.R: Sau bốn mươi ngày đi xem xét xứ, họ trở về.

decisions.choice: forty days
decisions.reason: The scouting lasts forty days, and in 14:34 the LORD sets the length of Israel's wandering by it: a year for each day, forty years in all. Forty is often a time of testing (Exodus 24:18; Deuteronomy 8:2).

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֡וּ וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־כָּל־עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־מִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָ֖ן קָדֵ֑שָׁה וַיָּשִׁ֨יבוּ אוֹתָ֤ם דָּבָר֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַיַּרְא֖וּם אֶת־פְּרִ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, to [the] wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and they brought back them word and all the congregation, and they showed them [the] fruit of the land.

en.L: And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. And they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and they showed them the fruit of the land.
en.B: They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They gave their report to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
en.R: They came back to Moses, Aaron and the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at Kadesh in the Paran Desert. They told them and all the people what they had found, and they showed them the fruit from the land.

es.L: Y fueron y vinieron a Moisés y a Aarón y a toda la comunidad de los hijos de Israel, al desierto de Parán, a Cades; y les trajeron respuesta a ellos y a toda la comunidad, y les mostraron el fruto de la tierra.
es.B: Volvieron adonde estaban Moisés, Aarón y toda la comunidad de los israelitas, en Cades, en el desierto de Parán. Les dieron su informe a ellos y a toda la comunidad, y les mostraron los frutos de la tierra.
es.R: Volvieron adonde estaban Moisés, Aarón y toda la comunidad de los israelitas, en Cades, en el desierto de Parán. Les contaron a ellos y a todo el pueblo lo que habían encontrado, y les mostraron los frutos de la tierra.

fr.L: Et ils allèrent et vinrent vers Moïse et vers Aaron et vers toute la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, au désert de Parân, à Kadesh. Et ils leur rapportèrent une parole, à eux et à toute la communauté, et ils leur montrèrent le fruit du pays.
fr.B: Ils revinrent auprès de Moïse, d’Aaron et de toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, à Kadesh, dans le désert de Parân. Ils leur firent leur rapport, à eux et à toute la communauté, et leur montrèrent les fruits du pays.
fr.R: Ils sont revenus auprès de Moïse, d’Aaron et de toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, à Kadesh, dans le désert de Parân. Ils leur ont raconté, à eux et à tout le peuple, ce qu’ils avaient trouvé, et ils leur ont montré les fruits du pays.

sw.L: Nao wakaenda wakafika kwa Musa na kwa Haruni na kwa jumuiya yote ya wana wa Israeli, katika nyika ya Parani, huko Kadeshi; wakawaletea habari wao na jumuiya yote, wakawaonyesha matunda ya nchi.
sw.B: Walirudi kwa Musa na Haruni na jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli huko Kadeshi katika nyika ya Parani. Wakawapa taarifa yao, wao na jumuiya yote, wakawaonyesha matunda ya nchi.
sw.R: Walirudi kwa Musa, Haruni na jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli huko Kadeshi katika jangwa la Parani. Wakawaeleza wao na watu wote yale waliyoyaona, wakawaonyesha matunda ya nchi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 가서 바란 광야 가데스로, 모세와 아론과 이스라엘 자손의 온 회중에게 왔다. 그리고 그들이 그들과 온 회중에게 소식을 전하고, 그들에게 그 땅의 열매를 보여 주었다.
ko.B: 그들은 바란 광야 가데스에 있는 모세와 아론과 이스라엘 백성의 온 회중에게 돌아왔다. 그들은 모세와 아론과 온 회중에게 보고하고, 그 땅의 열매를 보여 주었다.
ko.R: 그들은 바란 광야 가데스에 있는 모세와 아론과 이스라엘의 모든 사람에게 돌아왔다. 그들은 자기들이 보고 온 것을 모두에게 이야기하고, 그 땅에서 가져온 열매를 보여 주었다.

vi.L: Và họ đi và đến cùng Môi-se, cùng A-rôn và cùng cả hội chúng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, tại hoang mạc Pha-ran, ở Ca-đe. Và họ thuật lại cho họ và cho cả hội chúng, và cho họ xem trái cây của xứ.
vi.B: Họ trở về với Môi-se, A-rôn và cả hội chúng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên tại Ca-đe trong hoang mạc Pha-ran. Họ báo cáo cho hai ông và cho cả hội chúng, rồi cho họ xem trái cây của xứ.
vi.R: Họ trở về với Môi-se, A-rôn và toàn thể dân Y-sơ-ra-ên tại Ca-đe trong hoang mạc Pha-ran. Họ kể cho hai ông và mọi người nghe những gì họ đã thấy, rồi cho họ xem trái cây của xứ.

decisions.choice: Kadesh: the oasis of Kadesh-barnea, on the southern edge of Canaan
decisions.reason: Kadesh is called Kadesh-barnea in 32:8 and Deuteronomy 1:19. It lies where the wilderness of Paran meets the wilderness of Zin, which is why it is placed in Paran here and in Zin in 20:1 and 33:36.

decisions.choice: brought back word: reported
decisions.reason: "Bring back word" is the usual Hebrew way of saying that messengers report what they were sent to find out (Genesis 37:14; Joshua 14:7).

decisions.choice: all the people
decisions.reason: Readable says "community" for the congregation the first time and "all the people" the second, to avoid repeating the phrase.

decisions.choice: "hội chúng" (L, B); "toàn thể dân" (R); "hoang mạc"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for the congregation and the wilderness, as in Exodus; Readable uses the plain "toàn thể dân". Recorded once for chapters 12-18.

decisions.choice: "회중" for the congregation
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for *ʿedah* through Exodus to Deuteronomy; Readable says "모든 사람", as the English Readable says "all the people".

source.text: וַיְסַפְּרוּ־לוֹ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ בָּ֕אנוּ אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁלַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְ֠גַם זָבַ֨ת חָלָ֥ב וּדְבַ֛שׁ הִ֖וא וְזֶה־פִּרְיָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they recounted to him and said, We came to the land which you sent us, and also flowing of milk and honey [is] it, and this [is] its fruit.

en.L: And they told him and said, "We came to the land to which you sent us, and indeed it [is] flowing with milk and honey, and this [is] its fruit.
en.B: They gave Moses this account: "We went into the land you sent us to. It does flow with milk and honey, and here is its fruit.
en.R: They told Moses, "We went into the land where you sent us. It truly is a rich land, flowing with milk and honey. Here is some of its fruit.

es.L: Y le contaron y dijeron: «Fuimos a la tierra a la que nos enviaste, y en verdad [es una tierra] que fluye leche y miel, y este [es] su fruto.
es.B: Le dieron a Moisés este informe: «Entramos en la tierra adonde nos enviaste. De verdad es una tierra que fluye leche y miel, y aquí está su fruto.
es.R: Le contaron a Moisés: «Fuimos a la tierra adonde nos enviaste. De verdad es una tierra rica, que fluye leche y miel. Aquí tienes algunos de sus frutos.

fr.L: Et ils lui racontèrent et dirent : « Nous sommes allés dans le pays où tu nous as envoyés ; et vraiment c’est [un pays] où coulent le lait et le miel, et voici son fruit.
fr.B: Ils firent ce récit à Moïse : « Nous sommes allés dans le pays où tu nous as envoyés. C’est vraiment un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, et voici ses fruits.
fr.R: Ils ont dit à Moïse : « Nous sommes allés dans le pays où tu nous as envoyés. C’est vraiment un pays riche, un pays où coulent le lait et le miel. Voici quelques-uns de ses fruits.

sw.L: Nao wakamsimulia, wakasema, "Tuliingia katika nchi uliyotutuma; na kweli, inatiririka maziwa na asali, na haya [ndiyo] matunda yake.
sw.B: Wakampa Musa habari hii: "Tuliingia katika nchi uliyotutuma. Kweli ni nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, na haya ndiyo matunda yake.
sw.R: Walimwambia Musa, "Tuliingia katika nchi uliyotutuma. Kweli ni nchi tajiri, itiririkayo maziwa na asali. Haya ni baadhi ya matunda yake.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그에게 이야기하여 말했다. "우리가 당신이 우리를 보낸 그 땅에 갔습니다. 그리고 정말로 그 땅은 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 [땅]이며, 이것이 그 열매입니다.
ko.B: 그들이 모세에게 이렇게 보고했다. "우리는 당신이 우리를 보낸 그 땅에 들어가 보았습니다. 그곳은 정말 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅입니다. 이것이 그 땅의 열매입니다.
ko.R: 그들이 모세에게 말했다. "우리는 당신이 보낸 그 땅에 가 보았습니다. 그곳은 정말로 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 풍요로운 땅입니다. 여기 그 땅의 열매가 있습니다.

vi.L: Và họ thuật lại cho ông và nói: "Chúng tôi đã đến xứ mà ông đã sai chúng tôi đến, và quả thật xứ ấy tràn đầy sữa và mật, và đây [là] trái cây của nó.
vi.B: Họ thuật lại cho Môi-se: "Chúng tôi đã vào xứ mà ông sai chúng tôi đến. Xứ ấy quả thật tràn đầy sữa và mật, và đây là trái cây của xứ.
vi.R: Họ kể cho Môi-se: "Chúng tôi đã vào xứ ông sai chúng tôi đến. Đó thật là một xứ giàu có, tràn đầy sữa và mật. Đây là một ít trái cây của xứ ấy.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: rich and fruitful
decisions.reason: The saying describes a land with plenty: pasture for flocks that give milk, and honey, from wild bees or from the syrup of dates and other fruit. It is the LORD's own description of the land (Exodus 3:8, 17; 33:3). The scouts confirm it is true.

decisions.choice: and also: yes, it is so
decisions.reason: The small word "also" here confirms what had been promised: the land is just as it was said to be.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they told him", meaning Moses, who sent them (verse 3). Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: a rich land
decisions.reason: Readable adds "a rich land" to explain the saying while keeping its picture.

decisions.choice: The scouts call Moses "ông" and themselves "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for the people speaking to Moses and Aaron. Recorded once for chapters 12-18.

decisions.choice: "tràn đầy sữa và mật"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the land flowing with milk and honey.

decisions.choice: The scouts speak to Moses in 합쇼체 with "당신"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the people speak to Moses and Aaron in 합쇼체 with 당신 and 우리. The report of verses 27-33 is spoken before the whole congregation and keeps 합쇼체 throughout.

decisions.choice: "젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's phrase; Readable adds "풍요로운" (rich), as the English Readable does, to say what the picture means.

source.text: אֶ֚פֶס כִּֽי־עַ֣ז הָעָ֔ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהֶֽעָרִ֗ים בְּצֻר֤וֹת גְּדֹלֹת֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְגַם־יְלִדֵ֥י הָֽעֲנָ֖ק רָאִ֥ינוּ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: Only that strong [is] the people dwelling in the land, and the cities [are] fortified, great very; and also those born of the Anak we saw there.

en.L: Nevertheless, the people who dwell in the land [are] strong, and the cities [are] fortified [and] very large; and also we saw those born of Anak there.
en.B: But the people living in the land are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
en.R: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are very large and have strong walls. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.

es.L: Sin embargo, fuerte [es] el pueblo que habita en la tierra, y las ciudades [son] fortificadas, muy grandes; y también vimos allí a los nacidos de Anac.
es.B: Pero el pueblo que vive en esa tierra es poderoso, y las ciudades están fortificadas y son muy grandes. Hasta vimos allí a los descendientes de Anac.
es.R: Pero la gente que vive allí es fuerte, y sus ciudades son muy grandes y tienen murallas fuertes. Hasta vimos allí a los descendientes de Anac.

fr.L: Toutefois, le peuple qui habite dans le pays [est] fort, et les villes [sont] fortifiées, très grandes ; et aussi nous avons vu là ceux qui sont nés d’Anaq.
fr.B: Mais le peuple qui habite le pays est puissant, et les villes sont fortifiées et très grandes. Nous y avons même vu les descendants d’Anaq.
fr.R: Mais les gens qui vivent là sont forts, et leurs villes sont très grandes, avec de solides murailles. Nous y avons même vu des descendants d’Anaq.

sw.L: Lakini watu wanaokaa katika nchi [ni] hodari, na miji [ni] yenye ngome, mikubwa sana; na pia tuliwaona huko waliozaliwa na Anaki.
sw.B: Lakini watu wanaoishi katika nchi hiyo wana nguvu, na miji yao ina ngome na ni mikubwa sana. Hata tuliwaona huko wazao wa Anaki.
sw.R: Lakini watu wanaoishi huko wana nguvu, na miji yao ni mikubwa sana na ina kuta imara. Hata tuliwaona huko wazao wa Anaki.

ko.L: 그러나 그 땅에 사는 백성은 강하고, 성읍들은 요새화되어 있으며 매우 큽니다. 그리고 우리는 거기서 아낙의 자손들도 보았습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 그 땅에 사는 백성은 힘이 세고, 성읍들은 성벽이 둘러져 있고 매우 큽니다. 게다가 우리는 거기서 아낙 자손들까지 보았습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 그곳에 사는 사람들은 강합니다. 그들의 성읍은 아주 크고 튼튼한 성벽이 둘러져 있습니다. 우리는 거기서 아낙 자손들까지 보았습니다.

vi.L: Dầu vậy, dân cư ở trong xứ [thì] mạnh, và các thành [thì] kiên cố [và] rất lớn; và chúng tôi cũng đã thấy những người sinh ra từ A-nác tại đó.
vi.B: Nhưng dân sống trong xứ rất hùng mạnh, và các thành thì kiên cố và rất lớn. Chúng tôi còn thấy cả dòng dõi của A-nác ở đó nữa.
vi.R: Nhưng dân sống ở đó rất mạnh, và các thành của họ rất lớn, có tường vững chắc. Chúng tôi còn thấy cả dòng dõi của A-nác ở đó nữa.

decisions.choice: nevertheless: a strong turn against what was just said
decisions.reason: The scouts have confirmed the land is good. This word turns the report the other way: whatever the land is like, its people and cities make it look impossible to take. The answers to Moses' questions in verses 18-19 come out on the side of strength.

decisions.choice: fortified, very large: walled cities
decisions.reason: The word for fortified means cut off or made inaccessible, cities protected by walls. Deuteronomy 1:28 remembers the scouts saying the walls reached up to heaven.

decisions.choice: and also the descendants of Anak: the climax of the danger
decisions.reason: "And also" adds the worst news last: the Anakim of verse 22.

source.text: עֲמָלֵ֥ק יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַנֶּ֑גֶב וְ֠הַֽחִתִּי וְהַיְבוּסִ֤י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּהָ֔ר וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל־הַיָּ֔ם וְעַ֖ל יַ֥ד הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Amalek [is] dwelling in [the] land of the Negev, and the Hittite and the Jebusite and the Amorite [is] dwelling in the hill country, and the Canaanite [is] dwelling by the sea and by [the] side of the Jordan.

en.L: Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev, and the Hittite and the Jebusite and the Amorite dwell in the hill country, and the Canaanite dwells by the sea and along the side of the Jordan."

decisions.choice: Amalek, the Hittite, the Canaanite: whole peoples named in the singular
decisions.reason: Hebrew often names a people by a singular name, "the Canaanite" meaning the Canaanites as a whole.

decisions.choice: the peoples of the land
decisions.reason: The Amalekites were desert raiders who had already attacked Israel (Exodus 17:8-16). The Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites held the hill country; the Jebusites held Jerusalem (Joshua 15:63). The Hittites here are a people living in Canaan, as in Genesis 23, not the empire to the north. "Canaanite" names the people of the lowlands as well as the land's people in general.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: Set beside "the side of the Jordan", the sea is the western sea, the Mediterranean, the land's western border (34:6). The Canaanites hold the coastal plain in the west and the Jordan valley in the east (Joshua 5:1; 11:3).

decisions.choice: Amalekites, Hittites ... plural

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea ... the Jordan River

decisions.choice: quieted the people toward Moses: hushed people who were stirred up against Moses
decisions.reason: The verb means to say "hush" and silence someone. It implies the people had begun to murmur at the report, though the text does not record what they said. "Toward Moses" may mean in front of Moses, or that their noise was turned against him, as their complaint is in 14:2.

decisions.choice: going up we will go up ... being able we will be able: strong emphasis
decisions.reason: Twice Caleb doubles the verb, a Hebrew way of saying "certainly". His answer is as firm as the bad news: they can and should go.

decisions.choice: take possession of: take the land as their own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over and hold a land as an inheritance. It is the word used for Israel taking the promised land (Deuteronomy 1:8, 21).

decisions.choice: Let us go up, go up indeed
decisions.reason: Literal shows the doubled verb by repeating it. Balanced uses "must" and "surely" for the emphasis, and Readable keeps it plain.

decisions.choice: [to overcome] it / to conquer it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "we are able to it"; the sense is that they can overcome the land and its people.

decisions.choice: "chiếm lấy" for take possession
decisions.reason: To take the land as their own (meaning decision); "chiếm lấy" says it plainly and is used for the same verb through chapters 13-14.

decisions.choice: the men who had gone up with him: the other scouts, except Joshua
decisions.reason: "With him" refers to Caleb. Joshua sides with Caleb in 14:6-9, so the men meant here are the other ten (14:36-38).

decisions.choice: stronger than us
decisions.reason: The form can also be read "stronger than him", and an old Jewish reading took it as a claim that the people were stronger than God himself. The plain sense in the scouts' mouths is "than we are", matching "we are unable".

decisions.choice: go up against: attack
decisions.reason: "Go up" is the same verb Caleb used in verse 30, but with "against" it means to go up to fight. The scouts answer Caleb's "let us go up" with "we cannot go up".

decisions.choice: the other men

decisions.choice: brought out a bad report: spread an evil, slanderous account
decisions.reason: The word for "report" means an evil report, talk that harms someone (Genesis 37:2; Proverbs 10:18). In 14:36-37 the men who brought it die for it. Their report now speaks against the land itself, which they had called good in verse 27.

decisions.choice: a land that devours its inhabitants
alternatives: a land that cannot support its people
decisions.reason: The picture is of a land that eats up the people who live in it. It may mean that it is a land of constant war, where peoples fight over it and destroy each other, or that it is hard and deadly to live in. The scouts do not explain, and the claim goes against what they have just said about its fruit.

decisions.choice: men of stature: very tall men
decisions.reason: The word means measure or size. "Men of measures" are men of great height. Here the scouts say "all the people" are like this, more than they said in verse 28.

decisions.choice: [great]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "men of measures" needs a word in English to show the measure is large.

decisions.choice: eats up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of eating, in plain words, with the footnote giving the possible meanings.

decisions.choice: "loan ra ... một lời đồn xấu" (L, B); "nói ... những điều xấu" (R)
decisions.reason: They spread an evil, slanderous account (meaning decision); "lời đồn" carries the sense of a story spread among the people, more than a report to Moses.

decisions.choice: "nuốt chửng" for devours
decisions.reason: Vietnamese keeps the Hebrew picture, which the meaning decision footnotes; "nuốt chửng" is the everyday verb.

decisions.choice: "주민을 삼키는 땅" (L, B); "사람들을 잡아먹는 땅" (R)
decisions.reason: The picture is kept at every level, since its sense is disputed (meaning decision, footnoted); Readable uses the plainer verb.

decisions.choice: the Nephilim: the giants of the days before the flood
decisions.reason: The Nephilim are named elsewhere only in Genesis 6:4, as mighty men of old in the time before the flood. By calling the people of the land "Nephilim", the scouts make them sound like the giants of ancient stories, beings no one could stand against. Genesis 6:4 places them in the days before the flood, so the name shows how far the report has gone.

decisions.choice: the sons of Anak from the Nephilim: kept as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: These words explain who the Nephilim are by linking them with the Anakim of verses 22 and 28. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) does not have them; it reads only that the scouts saw the giants there. The Hebrew text is followed here. Reviewers should check this against a critical edition of the Septuagint.

decisions.choice: like grasshoppers in our eyes, and so in their eyes
decisions.reason: The scouts say they felt as small and weak as insects beside these people, and that the people of the land saw them the same way. They speak of what the people thought, though they had no way to know it; Rahab later says the people of the land were the ones afraid (Joshua 2:9-11).

decisions.choice: the giants
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Nephilim" as giants, from verse 32 and Genesis 6:4, and keeps the name.

decisions.choice: as small as grasshoppers / Next to them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the point of the comparison, size and weakness, and that it is beside these people that the scouts felt small.

decisions.choice: "saltamontes" for the grasshoppers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word here is not the one for the locusts of the plagues in Exodus 10, which this translation calls "langostas". "Saltamontes" is the small insect of everyday speech, which is the point of the comparison.

decisions.choice: "người Nê-phi-lim"
decisions.reason: The form of the Vietnamese Genesis 6:4; Readable adds "những người khổng lồ", as the English Readable says "the giants".

decisions.choice: "cào cào" for grasshoppers
decisions.reason: Both name the insect; "cào cào" is the common word for a small grasshopper and keeps the picture of smallness.

decisions.choice: "네피림", kept as a name
decisions.reason: The name as Genesis 6:4 gives it in Korean, so the allusion (meaning decision) is heard; Readable adds "거인들", as the English Readable adds "the giants".
